messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: egress-packetloss-euwest and bgp-route-oscillation triggered for prefixes served via Transit Provider AS65090. Symptoms: packet loss >5% from edges to Provider next-hops, BGP AS_PATH churn observed. Affected prefix cluster: 3.120.0.0/18. Pager sent to carla (oncall). Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/network-bgp

carla (oncall): I'm on pager. seeing increased error rates in eu-west: 502s up, p99 latency spike. KV cache miss rate +8% causing cold-starts. Starting triage — grabbing traceroutes + bgp tables.

carla (oncall): quick metrics snapshot: api-eu-ingress p99 520ms (baseline 90ms), kvcache hitrate 0.72 -> 0.66, edge egress packet loss 6-12% to AS65090 next-hops. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/d/xyz/eu-egress

carla (oncall): traceroute from eu-edge-02 to 3.120.45.12 (customer-host) shows loss at hop 6 (carrier peering).
```
traceroute to 3.120.45.12, 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  eu-edge-02 (10.10.2.3)  0.45 ms 0.31 ms 0.28 ms
 2  provider-agg1 (198.51.100.1)  1.2 ms 1.1 ms 1.3 ms
 3  provider-peering (203.0.113.10)  10.3 ms 11.0 ms 9.9 ms
 4  carrierx-hop (198.18.0.5)  24.5 ms 24.7 ms 24.6 ms  <-- packet loss spikes here
 5  carrierx-core (198.18.10.1)  25.3 ms  *  26.1 ms
 6  3.120.45.12  26.9 ms 27.1 ms 27.0 ms
```

bob (netops): I see BGP AS_PATH churn in our collectors: AS65090 is flapping prepends toward us on the /18 (multiple different prepends causing route selection churn). show bgp summary and updates show high update rate. Contacting CarrierX NOC now.

bob (netops): sample bgp update dump ->
```
BGP Update: prefix 3.120.0.0/18 AS_PATH: 65090 65090 65090 -> origin via peer A
BGP Update: prefix 3.120.0.0/18 AS_PATH: 65090 -> origin via peer B
(repeated oscillation, multiple unique next-hops observed in <1m window)
```

carla (oncall): Immediate mitigation options: 1) prefer alternate transit AS65501 via local-preference change to keep egress on stable path, 2) announce more specifics from eu-west (deaggregation) to steer inbound, 3) coordinate with CarrierX to stabilize. I prefer #1 + parallel coordination. Will coordinate with infra to apply route-map.

alice (eng-sre): FYI KV cache cold-starts are amplifying user-visible latency. If we can temporarily steer egress to stable transit the cache warmups will reduce. Also recommend turning on short-lived sticky routing for cache-pop endpoints to avoid thrashing between upstreams.

dave (infra): Preparing config change on tx-edge-01/02 to set route-map PREFER-ALT out to selected neighbor (203.0.113.5) which points at AS65501. Planning staged apply to avoid mass churn.

dave (infra): commands I'm going to run (FRR):
```
vtysh> configure terminal
router bgp 65001
 neighbor 203.0.113.5 route-map PREFER-ALT out
route-map PREFER-ALT permit 10
 set local-preference 200
exit
write memory
```

carla (oncall): applying on tx-edge-01 now. will monitor BGP update rate and packet loss.

elaine (support): drafting a brief customer's-facing status note for users seeing 502s in EU: "We're seeing intermittent network issues impacting EU requests; engineers are actively mitigating. If you're affected, please reply to this thread with request IDs." I'll post to status.redwood.ai once we have confirmation of mitigation.

frank (prod-eng): Also suggest reducing max_context_tokens for EU instances to reduce KV cache pressure while warmup happens. We'll roll config to 80% of EU requests with shorter context as a temporary mitigation.

bob (netops): CarrierX NOC responded: "We observed internal route flaps and a misconfigured prepending policy. Working on lockstep fixes. Recommend you steer traffic to alt peer while we stabilize."

carla (oncall): Traffic steering applied on tx-edge-01 and tx-edge-02. Observing BGP update rate drop ~40% and packet loss for affected paths down from 10% -> 2% to those next-hops. KV cache miss rate trending back toward baseline.

dave (infra): also announced /20 more-specifics from eu-west-edge-03 as a short-lived step to ensure stable customer sessions for the hottest prefixes. This is limited and will be withdrawn once CarrierX fixes.

alice (eng-sre): seeing application p99 drop to ~140ms and 502s reduce by ~70% for EU region. KV cache hitrate recovering. Good signs.

elaine (support): Posted customer status update: "We mitigated a network routing issue affecting EU traffic; reduced errors for most customers. Continued monitoring." Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incident/INC-1860

bob (netops): CarrierX confirms they deployed a fix on their fabric; no more prepends seen for the /18 in last 10m. Will keep monitoring BGP update delta.

carla (oncall): Monitoring for 30m stabilization window. If stable, we'll remove the temporary route-map and deaggregation.

carla (oncall): 30m check-in: BGP updates low, packet loss steady at <1%, app p99 steady. Proceeding to roll back traffic steering and withdraw /20 specifics in staged fashion.

carla (oncall): rollback complete on tx-edge-01/02/03. Confirming baseline.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: incident cleared. Classification: Infrastructure / Upstream transit BGP AS_PATH flapping caused egress packet loss and KV cache thrashing -> service errors for EU region. Mitigations applied: temporary local-pref to alternate transit, announced limited more-specifics, CarrierX corrected prepending policy. Postmortem assigned to bob (netops) + dave (infra). Follow-up: communicate RCA and permanent routing policy recommendations.

carla (oncall): handing off to bob for postmortem. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :team-heart:
notes: incident thread created by incident-bot and handled by on-call + netops; all messages are in chronological order
